comment: Logical-property enforcement over CSS. ESLint does not parse CSS at all, so until this
file existed a `margin-left` in src/index.css passed every gate in the repo in silence
(GAP §3, G-45). Stylelint's core rules are enough — no third-party plugin, and therefore
no extra supply-chain surface for a check this small.
The list is scoped to *direction-sensitive* declarations, which is the actual bug class:
`width` and `height` are the same axes in Hebrew, `margin-left` is not. `float` and
`clear` are banned by value rather than by property, because `float: inline-start` is the
correct spelling and the rule should not stand in its way.
Nothing else about CSS style is policed here; prettier already owns formatting and
Tailwind owns the utility layer. This config has exactly one job.
